items.followUp: Define a molecule and a cation.

accept: smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction
rubric.why: A valid definition identifies an atom as the smallest particle of an element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of an atom.

rubric.why: An ion is distinguished by having a net electric charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion is a charged atom or group of atoms.

modelAnswer: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction.
An ion is an atom or group of atoms that carries a net electric charge.

items.followUp: Differentiate between electron affinity and ionization energy.

rubric.why: Electron affinity describes the energy change when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.description: States the meaning of electron affinity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing electron affinity as the energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Electronegativity refers to attraction for shared electrons in a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing electronegativity as the tendency of a bonded atom to attract shared electrons.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom.
Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a chemical bond to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

items.followUp: Describe the trend in ionization energy down a group and give a reason.

rubric.why: The general trend across a period is an increase in ionization energy.
rubric.description: Gives the trend across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear attraction and decreasing atomic size make electron removal harder across a period.
rubric.description: Gives a valid reason for the trend.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased nuclear attraction or decreased atomic size to the higher energy needed to remove an electron.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Nuclear charge increases and atomic size generally decreases, so the outer electron is attracted more strongly to the nucleus and requires more energy to remove.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the property used to arrange elements in the modern periodic table.

rubric.why: Mendeleev's periodic law related the properties of elements to their atomic masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Mendeleev arranged elements according to atomic mass (or atomic weight).

rubric.why: The modern periodic law relates properties to atomic number rather than atomic mass.
rubric.description: States the modern periodic law basis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.
The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: What is a non-polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: Unequal sharing of the bonding electrons is what makes the covalent bond polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally.

rubric.why: Unequal sharing creates partial charges, or bond poles, due to different electronegativities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the unequal sharing produces partial positive and negative ends because the atoms attract electrons differently.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond becomes polar when the bonded atoms have different electronegativities and share the bonding electrons unequally.
This unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative ends in the bond.

items.followUp: Give two characteristic properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds have characteristic physical properties that result from their ions and strong electrostatic attractions.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic property of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct property, such as high melting or boiling point, crystalline nature, water solubility, brittleness, or electrical conduction when molten or in aqueous solution.

rubric.why: A second distinct characteristic property is required.
rubric.description: Gives a second characteristic property of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct property distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points because of the strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water because their ions are free to move.

items.followUp: Why are gases much more compressible than liquids?

rubric.why: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in a liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies the large spaces between gas particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas particles are widely separated or have large spaces between them.

rubric.why: Large particle spacing means less matter occupies a given volume, giving gases lower density.
rubric.description: Links particle spacing to lower density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the large spaces give gases less mass per unit volume (lower density) than liquids.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids, with large empty spaces between them.
Therefore, gases have less mass per unit volume and a lower density than liquids.

items.followUp: Define allotropy and give two forms of oxygen as an example.

rubric.why: Allotropy is the occurrence of an element in different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the same element exists in two or more different forms in the same physical state.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates allotropy in an element.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of allotropy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as diamond and graphite (carbon) or oxygen and ozone.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the existence of the same element in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
For example, carbon exists as diamond and graphite.
